full_judgment:
"The High Court Division founded is reasoning on the fact that the pre-emptor admittedly refused to buy a minor's property to avoid complication. In this respect, the Single Bench of the High Court Division was wrong because the legal position, as envisaged by section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 is that right to pre-emptive purchase accrues only after the property is sold, not before that, and that pre-emptive right does not exist, and is not enforceable before the sale, which principle is supported by the decision of this Division in Fazaruddin vs Mayejuddin arid others. 44 DLR (AD) 62."
